import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.Mahler32
/-!
# Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Mahler's Z-numbers

See also FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Mahler32.lean.

*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [Mah68] Mahler, Kurt. "An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2."
    Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 8.2 (1968): 313-321.
  - [FLP95] Flatto, Leopold, Jeffrey C. Lagarias, and Andrew D. Pollington.
    "On the range of fractional parts $\{\xi(p/q)^n\}$."
    Acta Arithmetica 70.2 (1995): 125-147.
-/

namespace Bugeaud09

/--
Problem 10.9. There are no real numbers $\xi$ such that $0 \le \{\xi (3/2)^n\} < 1/2$
for every positive integer $n$, i.e. no Z-number exists. Posed by Mahler [Mah68].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_9 : type_of% Mahler32.mahler_conjecture := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check: `1` is not a Z-number, since for `n = 1` we have
$\{1 \cdot (3/2)^1\} = \{3/2\} = 1/2 \not< 1/2$.
-/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_isZNumber_one : ¬ IsZNumber 1 := by
  rintro ⟨-, h⟩
  have h1 := h 1 le_rfl
  rw [pow_one, one_mul] at h1
  have hfr : Int.fract (3 / 2 : ℝ) = 1 / 2 := by rw [Int.fract]; norm_num [Int.floor_eq_iff]
  rw [hfr] at h1
  exact lt_irrefl _ h1

/--
Mahler [Mah68] proved that the set of Z-numbers has Lebesgue measure zero.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_9.variants.measure_zero :
    MeasureTheory.volume {ξ : ℝ | IsZNumber ξ} = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
Flatto, Lagarias, and Pollington [FLP95] proved that the set of Z-numbers has
Hausdorff dimension strictly less than $1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_9.variants.dimH_lt_one :
    dimH {ξ : ℝ | IsZNumber ξ} < 1 := by
  sorry

end Bugeaud09

findings.description: The docstring says there are no real numbers ξ satisfying the displayed fractional-part condition, without requiring ξ > 0. Literally this is false: ξ = 0 has fractional part 0 at every exponent. The Lean statement correctly excludes this case because IsZNumber ξ includes 0 < ξ. The omission reproduces the wording of Bugeaud’s Problem 10.9, rather than its intended Z-number interpretation.
findings.source_evidence: Bugeaud, Problem 10.9, p. 215, omits the positivity qualification, but Definition 3.2, p. 50, explicitly begins “A positive real number ξ is a Z-number.” Mahler (1968), p. 313, likewise begins with an arbitrary positive number before defining Z-numbers. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139017732.012 ; https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139017732.005 ; https://doi.org/10.1017/S1446788700005371 .
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to “There are no positive real numbers ξ such that …”, or explicitly state ξ > 0. Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The imported IsZNumber condition starts at n = 1, whereas Bugeaud’s Definition 3.2 and Mahler’s original definition start at n = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let Z₀(y) denote the positive-real Z-number condition for all n ≥ 0. Then IsZNumber ξ ↔ Z₀(ξ·3/2), by replacing n with n+1. Multiplication by 3/2 is a bijection on positive reals, so the nonexistence statements are equivalent. The omitted lower bound on the fractional part is automatic from Int.fract_nonneg.

reformulations.difference: The measured set uses the positive-exponent convention rather than Mahler’s zero-based convention.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing L for the Lean set and S for the original zero-based set, S = (ξ ↦ ξ·3/2) '' L. Consequently volume L = (2/3)·volume S, and nullity is equivalent in both conventions. This equivalence was proved without using the conjecture or the admitted size estimates.

reformulations.difference: The Hausdorff dimension is taken for the positive-exponent Z-number set rather than the zero-based set in FLP95.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two sets are carried to one another by multiplication by 3/2. This is a continuous linear equivalence, hence bi-Lipschitz, so their Hausdorff dimensions are equal. The equivalence of the strict dimension bounds was proved in Lean.

sources_consulted: Bugeaud (2012), Chapter 10, especially the introductory remarks and Problem 10.9, p. 215: https://static.cambridge.org/content/id/urn%3Acambridge.org%3Aid%3Abook%3A9781139017732/resource/name/9781139017732c10_p214-222_CBO.pdf

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the four Lean statements. Mahler proves countability, which implies both volume zero and, more strongly, Hausdorff dimension zero. FLP95 Theorem 1.1 also gives countability upon specializing to p=3, q=2, s=0, t=1/2, so the dimension variant is a valid corollary. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verify the reindexing equivalences, zero and endpoint cases, and the countability-to-size implications. They compile without errors or sorryAx dependencies; the existing test proof also has no sorryAx dependency. No repository files were modified.
